correctness.rationale: The determinant is primitive and linear in e with prime coefficient ac−b²; setting a=b=0 shows the other coefficient is not divisible by ac−b², in any characteristic. The six catalecticant minors satisfy AG−BE+CD=0 and the gradient is (G,−2E,C+3D,−2B,A). The displayed orthogonal-plane witness has rank four and independent reconstructed rows in every characteristic, proving generic reconstruction. When 2 is invertible, eliminating C gives 3D²−y₂D+y₁y₃/4−y₀y₄=0. If 3 is invertible too, the projection is finite and the smooth discriminant quadric has multiplicity one, so the affine-chart discriminant is not a function-field square and defines the branch divisor. In characteristic three the equation is generically linear in D. For the gradient ideal K=(A,B,C,E,G), D(a,b,d,e)⊂K by the four minor syzygies; D is not in the prime (a,b,d,e), so K=(K,D)∩(a,b,d,e). These two reduced projective pieces are disjoint. F vanishes on the quartic and is a unit locally at the extra point, so adding F leaves just the reduced quartic as the projective intrinsic singular scheme. In characteristic two two gradient coordinates vanish identically, proving the claimed image bound.
